newsitem.title: UK: Precious Metals Outlook -- Market calmer, for now.
newsitem.headline: Precious Metals Outlook -- Market calmer, for now.

text.p: Platinum and palladium (PGMs) have adopted a less frenzied tone as prices ease back from recent rally highs, but volatility will haunt the market until long-delayed Russian exports appear, dealers said.
The dearth of activity in the gold market, however, might prove a precursor to an imminent break-out -- more likely than not to the downside, analysts said.
The PGMs saw a touch of welcome liquidity last week, which helped calm the market after a severe supply squeeze produced near-panic at the start of the month.
The liquidity helped to ease concerns about the possibility of a default in the market, dealers said.

"Dealers have made an effort to restore order in spot trading. But no one wants to do anything if they can help it," a senior bullion trader said, adding that a modest amount of natural profit-taking and lending had entered the market.
Palladium had rocketed to 17-year highs two weeks ago and platinum traded at its highest in seven years amid a severe supply shortage exacerbated by a suspected fund-led squeeze.
Exports from key producer Russia, which produces 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 percent of its palladium, have been delayed for five months.
"Until the Russians start delivering metal to Japan it's not going to solve the liquidity problem. And even that is going to take a matter of months," a dealer said.
The market was kept on edge by fresh talk that Russian exports would be down sharply this year from last, traders said.

Dealers were also puzzling over reports from traders that officials of U.S.-based hedge fund Tiger Management -- believed to hold a massive amount of palladium through specualtive futures trade -- had visited Japan last week to sell the metal.
Still, amid more stable trading conditions, palladium was seen likely to consolidate on either side of the psychological $200 level, while platinum would find good support at $400.
From a technical standpoint, the PGMs were overheated and needed to correct lower, analysts said. Palladium had support at the $200 level, while platinum would find good support at $400.

"The very sharp rally we saw in platinum has broken some long term downtrends, removing the longer term downward pressure from the market," said technical analyst Cliff Green of Trend Analysis, adding that platinum was entering a broad consolidation phase.
Gold and silver have remained in the shadows of the PGMs, although analysts said they might be vulnerable to the downside after failing to progress higher with the PGMs in recent weeks.

Gold has been very narrowly range-bound above the $340 support area. Already quiet market may be knocked further by the presence of many dealers at the annual Financial Times gold conference in Prague this week.
The lack of upward momentum suggested the market might take another look at the recent low around $336, analysts said.
"The consolidation gold has seen since tumbling in February has been narrowing and is becoming more triangular," Green said.
"It appears to be coming to an apex of that triangle, signalling that the breakout will occur in the next month," he said, adding that the move would probably be to the downside.
